atoms.b: A coastal biome is a type of saltwater biome. This is where the ocean meets the ((Moon ++land)), and some of that land is submerged underwater.
A continental shelf is an area of ((plastic ++land)) that lies under the ocean and extends from the coastline to a drop-off point, where the deep ((mountain ++ocean)) starts.
Coastal biomes also include the water above the ((condensation ++continental)) shelf and the land that the sea covers during a high tide.

atoms.a: Coastal biomes are home to many different types of plants and animals.

feedback.end: This is because coastal biomes get lots of sunlight. The living things here include seaweed, fish, octopuses and much more.

atoms.text: Marine mangroves are a type of tree that often grow in tropical coastal biomes. There are around 80 different species of mangrove trees around the world.
Their underwater roots create the ideal environment for fish and other ocean wildlife to live in. Here, fish can find food and hide from larger predators.
Marine mangroves also act as a barrier to prevent erosion, which is when waves and tides gradually break down and carry away land.

atoms.a: What are the two ways in which mangroves are useful for our planet?
b: ++act as a barrier to prevent erosion
